Make JusPrin's "Your own API key" setup screen show whether a key is already saved, without revealing it. Repo: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin. Work in your own new worktree off jusprin-newui. Kenneth approved the design on 2026-10-21.

## The design (source of truth: the Claude canvas artifact; Figma is retired)
Canvas "JusPrin v2", https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v, page "Agent Setup · Empty State", board agent-setup-api-key-saved-vs-empty-proposal.dc.html ("api-key-field · saved vs empty · proposal"). Read it with the Artifact tool (action "read", path "project/agent-setup-api-key-saved-vs-empty-proposal.dc.html"); it is next to the existing setup-api-key boards. Five states:
1. **No key saved.** The field shows only placeholder text, "Paste your Anthropic key (sk-ant-…)" in text-tertiary, never bullets; "Paste" sits inside the field; Check key is disabled.
2. **Key saved.** A check icon (status-success) with "Key saved on this computer". The key is shown read-only as its start plus last 4 characters ("sk-ant-…a3F9") in the code style at full contrast, on a surface-subtle field, with "Replace" and "Remove" (Remove in status-danger). Below it: "JusPrin uses this key for every chat. Replace it to use another one."
3. **Replacing.** An empty, focused field (2 px border-focus) "Paste the new key", with Check key, Cancel and "Keeps sk-ant-…a3F9". The saved key stays until the new one passes its check; Cancel keeps it.
4. **Checking.** The saved key stays visible, with "Checking…" and Cancel.
5. **Key rejected.** A circle-alert icon with "The provider rejected this key" (status-danger), and the key field outlined in status-danger with Replace and Remove. Below it: "Replace it with a working key, or remove it."
The provider segmented control (Anthropic / OpenAI / Other…) stays at the top. Each provider shows its own state.

## Facts (verified 2026-10-20)
- Keys are stored per provider in the app's settings file as `<provider>_api_key` (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentConfiguration.cpp, api_key_item_for ~17 and load_provider_api_key ~40; the host already checks for a provider's key around line 103).
- The setup page always opens with an empty field: SetupApiKey in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/Setup.tsx (`useState('')` ~100), so a saved key and no key look the same today.
- No dates are stored for keys. Don't show "added" or "last used" dates, and don't add storage for them unless Kenneth asks.

## How
- The host sends the page, per provider, only whether a key is saved and a display hint: the key's prefix up to and including its first "-" segment(s) the provider uses (e.g. "sk-ant-") plus its last 4 characters. Never send the full key to the web page.
- Add it through the bridge (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts and the host side) as a capability, not a protocol version bump.
- Remove deletes the provider's key (and whatever cached Agent uses it; follow how setup already rebuilds or clears the Agent). Replace keeps the old key until the new one passes the existing check. Rejected comes from the existing check path when the saved key fails.
- Tokens only (resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json through CSS variables); read agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md "Writing UI code" and agent-docs/jusprin/README.md first. Read agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md before touching files outside src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/.
- Tests for the host (a key's hint never contains more than prefix + last 4; Remove clears it) and for the page (each of the five states). Fail-first for any new guard (restore from a saved copy, never `git checkout`).
- Capture the five states in the review page or the built app, light and dark, and send Kenneth the pictures.
- Don't use Kenneth's real stored keys in tests, and make no live AI model calls without his approval. Never print a key. Commit only when he asks.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). - init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

# Global Claude Code Rules

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.


## GCP / kubectl Credential Policy

Always use the service account `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for all `gcloud` and `kubectl` operations. Before running any such command, switch to it:

```bash
gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

The personal account `k@obico.io` is reserved for the user's own interactive CLI use and its OAuth tokens expire — do not rely on it.

## Sentry Access

- Instance: `sentry.obico.io`
- API base: `https://sentry.obico.io/api/0/`
- Auth token: `REDACTED`
- Usage: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" <api_url>`

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Overview

OrcaSlicer is an open-source 3D slicer application forked from Bambu Studio, built using C++ with wxWidgets for the GUI and CMake as the build system. The project uses a modular architecture with separate libraries for core slicing functionality, GUI components, and platform-specific code.

## Build Commands

### Building on Windows
```bash
# Build everything
build_release_vs2022.bat

# Build with debug symbols
build_release_vs2022.bat debug

# Build only dependencies
build_release_vs2022.bat deps

# Build only slicer (after deps are built)
build_release_vs2022.bat slicer


```

### Building on macOS
```bash
# Build everything (dependencies and slicer)
./build_release_macos.sh

# Build only dependencies
./build_release_macos.sh -d

# Build only slicer (after deps are built)
./build_release_macos.sh -s

# Use Ninja generator for faster builds
./build_release_macos.sh -x

# Build for specific architecture
./build_release_macos.sh -a arm64    # or x86_64 or universal

# Build for specific macOS version target
./build_release_macos.sh -t 11.3
```

### Building on Linux
```bash
# First time setup - install system dependencies
./build_linux.sh -u

# Build dependencies and slicer
./build_linux.sh -dsi

# Build everything (alternative)
./build_linux.sh -dsi

# Individual options:
./build_linux.sh -d    # dependencies only
./build_linux.sh -s    # slicer only  
./build_linux.sh -i    # build AppImage

# Performance and debug options:
./build_linux.sh -j N  # limit to N cores
./build_linux.sh -1    # single core build
./build_linux.sh -b    # debug build
./build_linux.sh -c    # clean build
./build_linux.sh -r    # skip RAM/disk checks
./build_linux.sh -l    # use Clang instead of GCC
```

### Build System
- Uses CMake with minimum version 3.13 (maximum 3.31.x on Windows)
- Primary build directory: `build/`
- Dependencies are built in `deps/build/`
- The build process is split into dependency building and main application building
- Windows builds use Visual Studio generators
- macOS builds use Xcode by default, Ninja with -x flag
- Linux builds use Ninja generator

### Testing
Tests are located in the `tests/` directory and use the Catch2 testing framework. Test structure:
- `tests/libslic3r/` - Core library tests (21 test files)
  - Geometry processing, algorithms, file formats (STL, 3MF, AMF)
  - Polygon operations, clipper utilities, Voronoi diagrams
- `tests/fff_print/` - Fused Filament Fabrication tests (12 test files)
  - Slicing algorithms, G-code generation, print mechanics
  - Fill patterns, extrusion, support material
- `tests/sla_print/` - Stereolithography tests (4 test files)
  - SLA-specific printing algorithms, support generation
- `tests/libnest2d/` - 2D nesting algorithm tests
- `tests/slic3rutils/` - Utility function tests
- `tests/sandboxes/` - Experimental/sandbox test code

Run all tests after building:
```bash
cd build && ctest
```

Run tests with verbose output:
```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure
```

Run individual test suites:
```bash
# From build directory
./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests
./tests/fff_print/fff_print_tests
./tests/sla_print/sla_print_tests
```

## Architecture

### Core Libraries
- **libslic3r/**: Core slicing engine and algorithms (platform-independent)
  - Main slicing logic, geometry processing, G-code generation
  - Key classes: Print, PrintObject, Layer, GCode, Config
  - Modular design with specialized subdirectories:
    - `GCode/` - G-code generation, cooling, pressure equalization, thumbnails
    - `Fill/` - Infill pattern implementations (gyroid, honeycomb, lightning, etc.)
    - `Support/` - Tree supports and traditional support generation
    - `Geometry/` - Advanced geometry operations, Voronoi diagrams, medial axis
    - `Format/` - File I/O for 3MF, AMF, STL, OBJ, STEP formats
    - `SLA/` - SLA-specific print processing and support generation
    - `Arachne/` - Advanced wall generation using skeletal trapezoidation

- **src/slic3r/**: Main application framework and GUI
  - GUI application built with wxWidgets
  - Integration between libslic3r core and user interface
  - Located in `src/slic3r/GUI/` (not shown in this directory but exists)

### Key Algorithmic Components
- **Arachne Wall Generation**: Variable-width perimeter generation using skeletal trapezoidation
- **Tree Supports**: Organic support generation algorithm  
- **Lightning Infill**: Sparse infill optimization for internal structures
- **Adaptive Slicing**: Variable layer height based on geometry
- **Multi-material**: Multi-extruder and soluble support processing
- **G-code Post-processing**: Cooling, fan control, pressure advance, conflict checking

### File Format Support
- **3MF/BBS_3MF**: Native format with extensions for multi-material and metadata
- **STL**: Standard tessellation language for 3D models
- **AMF**: Additive Manufacturing Format with color/material support  
- **OBJ**: Wavefront OBJ with material definitions
- **STEP**: CAD format support for precise geometry
- **G-code**: Output format with extensive post-processing capabilities

### External Dependencies
- **Clipper2**: Advanced 2D polygon clipping and offsetting
- **libigl**: Computational geometry library for mesh operations
- **TBB**: Intel Threading Building Blocks for parallelization
- **wxWidgets**: Cross-platform GUI framework
- **OpenGL**: 3D graphics rendering and visualization
- **CGAL**: Computational Geometry Algorithms Library (selective use)
- **OpenVDB**: Volumetric data structures for advanced operations
- **Eigen**: Linear algebra library for mathematical operations

## File Organization

### Resources and Configuration
- `resources/profiles/` - Printer and material profiles organized by manufacturer
- `resources/printers/` - Printer-specific configurations and G-code templates  
- `resources/images/` - UI icons, logos, calibration images
- `resources/calib/` - Calibration test patterns and data
- `resources/handy_models/` - Built-in test models (benchy, calibration cubes)

### Internationalization and Localization  
- `localization/i18n/` - Source translation files (.pot, .po)
- `resources/i18n/` - Runtime language resources
- Translation managed via `scripts/run_gettext.sh` / `scripts/run_gettext.bat`

### Platform-Specific Code
- `src/libslic3r/Platform.cpp` - Platform abstractions and utilities
- `src/libslic3r/MacUtils.mm` - macOS-specific utilities (Objective-C++)
- Windows-specific build scripts and configurations
- Linux distribution support scripts in `scripts/linux.d/`

### Build and Development Tools
- `cmake/modules/` - Custom CMake find modules and utilities
- `scripts/` - Python utilities for profile generation and validation  
- `tools/` - Windows build tools (gettext utilities)
- `deps/` - External dependency build configurations

## Development Workflow

### Code Style and Standards
- **C++17 standard** with selective C++20 features
- **Naming conventions**: PascalCase for classes, snake_case for functions/variables
- **Header guards**: Use `#pragma once` 
- **Memory management**: Prefer smart pointers, RAII patterns
- **Thread safety**: Use TBB for parallelization, be mindful of shared state

### Common Development Tasks

#### Adding New Print Settings
1. Define setting in `PrintConfig.cpp` with proper bounds and defaults
2. Add UI controls in appropriate GUI components  
3. Update serialization in config save/load
4. Add tooltips and help text for user guidance
5. Test with different printer profiles

#### Modifying Slicing Algorithms  
1. Core algorithms live in `libslic3r/` subdirectories
2. Performance-critical code should be profiled and optimized
3. Consider multi-threading implications (TBB integration)
4. Validate changes don't break existing profiles
5. Add regression tests where appropriate

#### GUI Development
1. GUI code resides in `src/slic3r/GUI/` (not visible in current tree)
2. Use existing wxWidgets patterns and custom controls
3. Support both light and dark themes
4. Consider DPI scaling on high-resolution displays
5. Maintain cross-platform compatibility

#### Adding Printer Support
1. Create JSON profile in `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`
2. Add printer-specific start/end G-code templates
3. Configure build volume, capabilities, and material compatibility
4. Test thoroughly with actual hardware when possible
5. Follow existing profile structure and naming conventions

### Dependencies and Build System
- **CMake-based** with separate dependency building phase
- **Dependencies** built once in `deps/build/`, then linked to main application  
- **Cross-platform** considerations important for all changes
- **Resource files** embedded at build time, platform-specific handling

### Performance Considerations
- **Slicing algorithms** are CPU-intensive, profile before optimizing
- **Memory usage** can be substantial with complex models
- **Multi-threading** extensively used via TBB
- **File I/O** optimized for large 3MF files with embedded textures
- **Real-time preview** requires efficient mesh processing

## Important Development Notes

### Codebase Navigation
- Use search tools extensively - codebase has 500k+ lines
- Key entry points: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp` for application startup
- Core slicing: `libslic3r/Print.cpp` orchestrates the slicing pipeline
- Configuration: `PrintConfig.cpp` defines all print/printer/material settings

### Compatibility and Stability
- **Backward compatibility** maintained for project files and profiles
- **Cross-platform** support essential (Windows/macOS/Linux)  
- **File format** changes require careful version handling
- **Profile migrations** needed when settings change significantly

### Quality and Testing
- **Regression testing** important due to algorithm complexity
- **Performance benchmarks** help catch performance regressions
- **Memory leak** detection important for long-running GUI application
- **Cross-platform** testing required before releases

When the user asks to commit changes:

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Overview

OrcaSlicer is an open-source 3D slicer application forked from Bambu Studio, built using C++ with wxWidgets for the GUI and CMake as the build system. The project uses a modular architecture with separate libraries for core slicing functionality, GUI components, and platform-specific code.

## Build Commands

### Building on Windows
```bash
# Build everything
build_release_vs2022.bat

# Build with debug symbols
build_release_vs2022.bat debug

# Build only dependencies
build_release_vs2022.bat deps

# Build only slicer (after deps are built)
build_release_vs2022.bat slicer


```

### Building on macOS
```bash
# Build everything (dependencies and slicer)
./build_release_macos.sh

# Build only dependencies
./build_release_macos.sh -d

# Build only slicer (after deps are built)
./build_release_macos.sh -s

# Use Ninja generator for faster builds
./build_release_macos.sh -x

# Build for specific architecture
./build_release_macos.sh -a arm64    # or x86_64 or universal

# Build for specific macOS version target
./build_release_macos.sh -t 11.3
```

### Building on Linux
```bash
# First time setup - install system dependencies
./build_linux.sh -u

# Build dependencies and slicer
./build_linux.sh -dsi

# Build everything (alternative)
./build_linux.sh -dsi

# Individual options:
./build_linux.sh -d    # dependencies only
./build_linux.sh -s    # slicer only  
./build_linux.sh -i    # build AppImage

# Performance and debug options:
./build_linux.sh -j N  # limit to N cores
./build_linux.sh -1    # single core build
./build_linux.sh -b    # debug build
./build_linux.sh -c    # clean build
./build_linux.sh -r    # skip RAM/disk checks
./build_linux.sh -l    # use Clang instead of GCC
```

### Build System
- Uses CMake with minimum version 3.13 (maximum 3.31.x on Windows)
- Primary build directory: `build/`
- Dependencies are built in `deps/build/`
- The build process is split into dependency building and main application building
- Windows builds use Visual Studio generators
- macOS builds use Xcode by default, Ninja with -x flag
- Linux builds use Ninja generator

### Testing
Tests are located in the `tests/` directory and use the Catch2 testing framework. Test structure:
- `tests/libslic3r/` - Core library tests (21 test files)
  - Geometry processing, algorithms, file formats (STL, 3MF, AMF)
  - Polygon operations, clipper utilities, Voronoi diagrams
- `tests/fff_print/` - Fused Filament Fabrication tests (12 test files)
  - Slicing algorithms, G-code generation, print mechanics
  - Fill patterns, extrusion, support material
- `tests/sla_print/` - Stereolithography tests (4 test files)
  - SLA-specific printing algorithms, support generation
- `tests/libnest2d/` - 2D nesting algorithm tests
- `tests/slic3rutils/` - Utility function tests
- `tests/sandboxes/` - Experimental/sandbox test code

Run all tests after building:
```bash
cd build && ctest
```

Run tests with verbose output:
```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure
```

Run individual test suites:
```bash
# From build directory
./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests
./tests/fff_print/fff_print_tests
./tests/sla_print/sla_print_tests
```

## Architecture

### Core Libraries
- **libslic3r/**: Core slicing engine and algorithms (platform-independent)
  - Main slicing logic, geometry processing, G-code generation
  - Key classes: Print, PrintObject, Layer, GCode, Config
  - Modular design with specialized subdirectories:
    - `GCode/` - G-code generation, cooling, pressure equalization, thumbnails
    - `Fill/` - Infill pattern implementations (gyroid, honeycomb, lightning, etc.)
    - `Support/` - Tree supports and traditional support generation
    - `Geometry/` - Advanced geometry operations, Voronoi diagrams, medial axis
    - `Format/` - File I/O for 3MF, AMF, STL, OBJ, STEP formats
    - `SLA/` - SLA-specific print processing and support generation
    - `Arachne/` - Advanced wall generation using skeletal trapezoidation

- **src/slic3r/**: Main application framework and GUI
  - GUI application built with wxWidgets
  - Integration between libslic3r core and user interface
  - Located in `src/slic3r/GUI/` (not shown in this directory but exists)

### Key Algorithmic Components
- **Arachne Wall Generation**: Variable-width perimeter generation using skeletal trapezoidation
- **Tree Supports**: Organic support generation algorithm  
- **Lightning Infill**: Sparse infill optimization for internal structures
- **Adaptive Slicing**: Variable layer height based on geometry
- **Multi-material**: Multi-extruder and soluble support processing
- **G-code Post-processing**: Cooling, fan control, pressure advance, conflict checking

### File Format Support
- **3MF/BBS_3MF**: Native format with extensions for multi-material and metadata
- **STL**: Standard tessellation language for 3D models
- **AMF**: Additive Manufacturing Format with color/material support  
- **OBJ**: Wavefront OBJ with material definitions
- **STEP**: CAD format support for precise geometry
- **G-code**: Output format with extensive post-processing capabilities

### External Dependencies
- **Clipper2**: Advanced 2D polygon clipping and offsetting
- **libigl**: Computational geometry library for mesh operations
- **TBB**: Intel Threading Building Blocks for parallelization
- **wxWidgets**: Cross-platform GUI framework
- **OpenGL**: 3D graphics rendering and visualization
- **CGAL**: Computational Geometry Algorithms Library (selective use)
- **OpenVDB**: Volumetric data structures for advanced operations
- **Eigen**: Linear algebra library for mathematical operations

## File Organization

### Resources and Configuration
- `resources/profiles/` - Printer and material profiles organized by manufacturer
- `resources/printers/` - Printer-specific configurations and G-code templates  
- `resources/images/` - UI icons, logos, calibration images
- `resources/calib/` - Calibration test patterns and data
- `resources/handy_models/` - Built-in test models (benchy, calibration cubes)

### Internationalization and Localization  
- `localization/i18n/` - Source translation files (.pot, .po)
- `resources/i18n/` - Runtime language resources
- Translation managed via `scripts/run_gettext.sh` / `scripts/run_gettext.bat`

### Platform-Specific Code
- `src/libslic3r/Platform.cpp` - Platform abstractions and utilities
- `src/libslic3r/MacUtils.mm` - macOS-specific utilities (Objective-C++)
- Windows-specific build scripts and configurations
- Linux distribution support scripts in `scripts/linux.d/`

### Build and Development Tools
- `cmake/modules/` - Custom CMake find modules and utilities
- `scripts/` - Python utilities for profile generation and validation  
- `tools/` - Windows build tools (gettext utilities)
- `deps/` - External dependency build configurations

## Development Workflow

### Code Style and Standards
- **C++17 standard** with selective C++20 features
- **Naming conventions**: PascalCase for classes, snake_case for functions/variables
- **Header guards**: Use `#pragma once`

Two private artifacts in Kenneth's Claude account mirror the Figma file
([[figma-jusprin-v2-file]]). Since 2026-10-20 these artifacts ARE the source of truth ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]); edit them directly. The Figma re-sync steps below are history.

1. Design System: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL (version 9)
   - `tokens.json` + `tokens.css`, 37 coded React components (`window.JusPrin`).
   - Each component card: every variant Figma draws, a Light and a Dark panel,
     then the coded component. The page lists them as one flat table in bundle
     order with code names; it draws no group headings.
   - `screens/<page>/<screen>.spec.txt` (166) + `screens/index.json`: plain
     files for agents, one resolved line per layer.
2. Design canvas "JusPrin v2": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
   (version 7): 10 pages with Figma's names in Figma's order, 198 artboards at
   their Figma x,y and in Figma's layer order, each drawn in the Light or Dark
   mode Figma sets on it; "… · Light & Dark" review frames are drawn whole.

Tools, reads and backups are durable now, outside the repo:
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/` — start with
its `README.md` (step-by-step re-sync). `published/` is an exact copy of what is
live; `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` holds the earlier state with the
scripts that reproduce it byte for byte.

How Kenneth wants a re-sync done (2026-10-13): back up first, re-import, then
compare the backup with the new import so nothing already in sync regresses.
The method that worked, in order:
- rebuild from the old reads and require byte-identical output (proves the
  scripts);
- re-read Figma with the old script and diff the reads (proves Figma unchanged:
  all 14 files were identical);
- only then change scripts, and explain every file `compare_builds.py` reports;
- score every artboard against Figma's own page screenshots
  (`visual_compare.py`) and allow no artboard to score worse.
Result of that run: 0 artboards further from Figma, 36 closer; boards within 5
of Figma (0–255 scale) went from 99 to 122 of 186; all 37 cards and 163 of 166
spec files came out byte-identical; tokens matched Figma's variables exactly.

What the screenshot comparison caught that file checks could not: dark panels I
had added behind dark variants (Figma has none), frames forced dark by a "dark"
in their name (use Figma's `explicitVariableModes` instead), a frame half light
and half dark through a nested mode, sets whose background is a two-stop linear
gradient, Figma's GRID layout (children need their own positions), and small

description: "Agent tool isolation:\"worktree\" cut worktrees from a stale base and SendMessage was disabled; create worktrees by hand on the intended commit and pass absolute paths"
metadata:

---

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
was the only option.

**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

name: bash-cwd-resets-after-background
description: "The Bash tool's working directory silently reverts to the primary repo after a run_in_background command or a failed cd; worktree commands must cd explicitly or use absolute paths."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 3bfe66db-4c50-4102-b9b3-5ec3eab0060d
  modified: 2026-09-02T18:12:49.419Z
---

While working in a git worktree, a later `cmake --build build/arm64` and a
`git status` ran in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin` (the main checkout)
instead of the worktree, so one build reported "no work to do" and a status
check looked as if every edit had been lost.

**Why:** After a `run_in_background` Bash call, and after a compound command
whose `cd` failed, the session cwd is the primary working directory again.
The tool result even says so, but it is easy to miss in a long session.

**How to apply:** In worktree sessions start every Bash command with
`cd <worktree> &&`, or use absolute paths everywhere (python patch scripts
with an absolute root are safest). Verify with `pwd` before trusting a
`git status` that looks wrong. See [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

description: "Agent tool isolation:\"worktree\" cut worktrees from a stale base and SendMessage was disabled; create worktrees by hand on the intended commit and pass absolute paths"
metadata:

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
was the only option.

**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

name: bash-cwd-resets-after-background
description: "The Bash tool's working directory silently reverts to the primary repo after a run_in_background command or a failed cd; worktree commands must cd explicitly or use absolute paths."
metadata:

  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 3bfe66db-4c50-4102-b9b3-5ec3eab0060d
  modified: 2026-09-02T18:12:49.419Z

While working in a git worktree, a later `cmake --build build/arm64` and a
`git status` ran in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin` (the main checkout)
instead of the worktree, so one build reported "no work to do" and a status
check looked as if every edit had been lost.

**Why:** After a `run_in_background` Bash call, and after a compound command
whose `cd` failed, the session cwd is the primary working directory again.
The tool result even says so, but it is easy to miss in a long session.

**How to apply:** In worktree sessions start every Bash command with
`cd <worktree> &&`, or use absolute paths everywhere (python patch scripts
with an absolute root are safest). Verify with `pwd` before trusting a

name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

name: agent-setup-api-key-path
description: "JusPrin Agent setup, API-key route — verification-is-construction design, privacy rule for the probe, and the routes deliberately left unbuilt."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: eb922e6b-d324-4167-adb6-c08ea83efb8f
  modified: 2026-09-14T16:29:41.120Z
---

Commit `d4012fe1df` on `jusprin-newui` (2026-09-01) built the API-key route of
Agent setup, the destination of the previously inert "Set up the agent" button
from `454e9a1b5f`. Design came from the Figma file **JusPrin v2**, page
"Agent Setup - Empty State" (5 frames); since 2026-10-20 the up-to-date version of that page is the
"Agent Setup · Empty State" page of the JusPrin v2 canvas artifact ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]). See [[agent-bridge-phase-5]] for the
preceding phase.

**Verification and construction are the same act.** `ProviderKeySetup` checks a
key by running one real request through the same `OpenAIResponsesAgent` the
Agent will use, and hands that already-connected instance back as the outcome.
A key that passes cannot drift apart from an Agent that works, and the
"replied in 0.8 s" shown is the measurement that happened. Prefer this over a
separate validation call if this is ever extended to another provider.

**The probe carries no project data.** It sends a fixed sentence and an empty
workspace snapshot: a provider the user has not chosen yet must not receive
their workspace just to prove a key works. A test asserts this.

Structure: setup is poll-driven like `IAgentService` so `AgentHost` stays
deterministic; the probe is GUI-free and unit-testable; the commit step
(AppConfig only; the key is `jusprin_agent.openai_api_key` since 2026-09-14, moved out of the Keychain because every unsigned rebuild re-prompted) is injected from `AgentConfiguration.cpp`, which is also
where completing the flow records `cloud_consent`. Threaded through as
`AgentRuntime::setup`. Protocol grew `setup_check_key` / `setup_cancel` /
`setup_status` under an `agent_setup` capability, no version bump — see
[[protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary]].

**Deliberately not built, in priority order:** an Anthropic adapter (so the
design's default tab is disabled and the screen opens on OpenAI); the "Other…"
provider (meaning undefined); "Continue with JusPrin" (no account backend
exists in the repo — needs the auth endpoint, flow shape, and whether the app
receives a JusPrin token or a provider key); "Run a model on this machine"
(needs a JusPrin MCP server that may not exist, and a download source to
confirm before writing code that fetches a binary).

Testing this path: the shell harness points `JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` at a
closed local port so the real host, page, and HTTP transport are exercised
without an external service — that covers the failure path only. For a real
key, `--manual-unconfigured` (see [[jusprin-shell-manual-harness]]). The key now lives in the harness's AppConfig, so it does not survive runs;
an old `JusPrin Agent OpenAI` Keychain entry is ignored.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

name: never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree
description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: cb4c8804-b0a0-4ca0-b4a5-6b6998947d4b
  modified: 2026-09-24T00:36:34.672Z
---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

name: fake-host-page-fixture
description: "Render the built AgentUI/HomeUI bundles in the built-in browser with a scripted fake native host, to see page states the live app makes hard to catch"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 9bb21a20-a19f-4500-adcf-139798a1201d
  modified: 2026-09-19T16:55:23.039Z

Both pages find their host through `window.wx.postMessage(json)` and receive host
envelopes through `window.__jusprinBridge.deliver(envelope)` (`WebShared/bridgeClient.ts`).
Copy `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject
`<script>` right after `<head>` that (1) defines `window.wx` answering `hello` with
`hello_ack` + a full `state`, and (2) exposes `window.fake.deliver(type, payload)`;
serve with `python3 -m http.server` and open `agent.html?panel=printer` /
`home.html` via `preview_start`. Drive it with `javascript_tool`: deliver
`assistant_started` with no `assistant_delta` to freeze a streaming empty turn,
`printer_session` to pin a card, `printer_added` for Home's receipt strip. A file
drop works with `new DragEvent('drop', {dataTransfer})` on `.app--printer`.
Envelope: `{protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge'|'jusprin-home-bridge', version:1, id, type, payload}`.
Used 2026-09-19 to review branch these-commits-are-probably-wrong in ~10 minutes.

**Why:** the desktop tools were locked by another session and background
`app_click` never reaches WKWebView content, so page-level states (streaming
activity line, compact photo chip, leave dialog, receipt strip) had no other cheap
proof. It proves page rendering only; host behaviour (e.g. the 256 KiB image
preview cap `kInlineImagePreviewCap` in `AgentHost.cpp`) must be replicated in
the fake by hand or checked live.

**How to apply:** reach for this before building a full app + datadir copy when the
question is "what does the page draw for state X". Pair with [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]]
for the host side. Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

name: screenshots-to-files-via-page-fixture
description: "computer_batch save_to_disk produced no files (2026-09-23); to get screenshot files for a report, replay the observed host state into the built Agent/Home page under Playwright, which saves PNGs; plus the window-overlap trap when another session runs the harness."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 49ad3806-419d-49f2-8833-1578cd5bf2b3
  modified: 2026-09-23T21:16:58.377Z
---

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

name: protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary
description: "Agent-bridge protocol version is pinned at 1 pre-release; add features via the capabilities list, never a version bump."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 05ae687e-7468-4101-ba4b-f0017c8876c5
  modified: 2026-09-01T07:39:46.979Z
---

For the JusPrin agent bridge, do NOT increment the protocol version integer for additive changes (new message types, new capabilities), and especially not before the product is released.

**Why:** the version integer exists only so a running web page and native host can detect they are incompatible. They are built together and baked into the same binary (the bundle ships inside `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` in the same build as the host), and nothing is released — so no older peer exists that a version bump could protect. Feature detection is the job of the `capabilities` list, and additive changes are backward-compatible by construction.

**Baseline:** the version is pinned at **1** and stays 1 through all pre-release development. It bumps only after go-live, on a breaking change to an existing message's shape. (Kenny's call, 2026-09-01: the per-phase v1→v2→v3 bumps were all churn, so it was reset to 1.)

**How to apply:** add the new capability to `capabilities` (in `protocol.json`, `AgentProtocol.hpp`, and `protocol.ts` — the contract test checks all three agree) and the new message-type constants; leave `kVersion` at 1. Note `state.json` has its own separate `ProjectStateDocument::kSchemaVersion` — that IS a real persistence-compatibility concern (saved 3mf opened by another build) and is unrelated to this protocol version; don't conflate them.

In `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`, `import css from './styles.css?raw'` under Vitest resolves to an empty string, and `new URL('./x', import.meta.url)` is not a `file:` URL in the jsdom environment. A stylesheet-guard test written either way passed green while asserting nothing.

**Why:** Vitest's CSS handling short-circuits the import before Vite's `?raw` asset path runs, so every regex over the "stylesheet" matched nothing. Only appending a deliberate `border-radius: 4px` to the file and watching the suite stay green exposed it.

**How to apply:** Read source files in tests with `readFileSync(join(__dirname, ...))` and assert the text is non-empty. For any guard test that scans a file, inject the violation it exists to catch, confirm it fails naming the offender, then restore. name: agent-panel-css-namespaces
description: AgentUI styles.css has no CSS modules — the setup-* class prefix belongs to the agent setup screens, so new components need their own prefix

suites stayed green — jsdom does no layout, so no unit test can see it.

(`grep -n '^\.<prefix>' src/styles.css`), and verify layout by rendering the
real component at real width rather than trusting tests. The pattern that
works: `SetupCard.preview.test.tsx` uses `renderToStaticMarkup` plus the real
styles.css and design tokens to emit a page of every state, served over a
local http server and measured in the browser (`scrollWidth > clientWidth`,
row heights). See [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

Commit `d4012fe1df` on `jusprin-newui` (2026-09-01) built the API-key route of
Agent setup, the destination of the previously inert "Set up the agent" button
from `454e9a1b5f`. Design came from the Figma file **JusPrin v2**, page
"Agent Setup - Empty State" (5 frames); since 2026-10-20 the up-to-date version of that page is the
"Agent Setup · Empty State" page of the JusPrin v2 canvas artifact ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]). See [[agent-bridge-phase-5]] for the

**Verification and construction are the same act.** `ProviderKeySetup` checks a
key by running one real request through the same `OpenAIResponsesAgent` the
Agent will use, and hands that already-connected instance back as the outcome.
A key that passes cannot drift apart from an Agent that works, and the
"replied in 0.8 s" shown is the measurement that happened. Prefer this over a
separate validation call if this is ever extended to another provider.

**The probe carries no project data.** It sends a fixed sentence and an empty
workspace snapshot: a provider the user has not chosen yet must not receive
their workspace just to prove a key works. A test asserts this.

Structure: setup is poll-driven like `IAgentService` so `AgentHost` stays
deterministic; the probe is GUI-free and unit-testable; the commit step

description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06

---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

name: never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree
description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: cb4c8804-b0a0-4ca0-b4a5-6b6998947d4b
  modified: 2026-09-24T00:36:34.672Z
---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

description: "computer_batch save_to_disk produced no files (2026-09-23); to get screenshot files for a report, replay the observed host state into the built Agent/Home page under Playwright, which saves PNGs; plus the window-overlap trap when another session runs the harness."

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

name: protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary
description: "Agent-bridge protocol version is pinned at 1 pre-release; add features via the capabilities list, never a version bump."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 05ae687e-7468-4101-ba4b-f0017c8876c5
  modified: 2026-09-01T07:39:46.979Z
---

For the JusPrin agent bridge, do NOT increment the protocol version integer for additive changes (new message types, new capabilities), and especially not before the product is released.

**Why:** the version integer exists only so a running web page and native host can detect they are incompatible. They are built together and baked into the same binary (the bundle ships inside `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` in the same build as the host), and nothing is released — so no older peer exists that a version bump could protect. Feature detection is the job of the `capabilities` list, and additive changes are backward-compatible by construction.

**Baseline:** the version is pinned at **1** and stays 1 through all pre-release development. It bumps only after go-live, on a breaking change to an existing message's shape. (Kenny's call, 2026-09-01: the per-phase v1→v2→v3 bumps were all churn, so it was reset to 1.)

**How to apply:** add the new capability to `capabilities` (in `protocol.json`, `AgentProtocol.hpp`, and `protocol.ts` — the contract test checks all three agree) and the new message-type constants; leave `kVersion` at 1. Note `state.json` has its own separate `ProjectStateDocument::kSchemaVersion` — that IS a real persistence-compatibility concern (saved 3mf opened by another build) and is unrelated to this protocol version; don't conflate them.

`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.css` is one flat global stylesheet
